summary: Extension authors adding new database backends or custom catalog implementations. Primary contracts: Backend protocol (structural), DialectSpec (Ibis), IcebergConnectionBase (Iceberg), @register decorator (settings). No inheritance required for Ibis backends.

concepts.name: Backend protocol contract
recommended_docs: Backend is a structural protocol — no inheritance needed, just implement the interface
Required: name str, connect(), close(), __enter__/__exit__, list_tables(), list_namespaces(), inspect_table(), inspect_namespace(), inspect_catalog()

concepts.name: Adding an Ibis dialect extension
recommended_docs: Add to DIALECTS dict: DialectSpec(ibis_backend_name=..., connection_mode=..., connection_string_scheme=..., connection_builder=callable)
Optional hooks: upsert_hook, create_index_hook, drop_index_hook, rename_table_hook, get_index_exists_sql, get_list_indexes_sql

concepts.name: Adding a settings class for a new backend
recommended_docs: Optionally set __adapter__ = my_adapter_callable for complex kwarg mapping
evidence: Per-backend settings files (e.g. sqlite.py) as two-line pattern reference

concepts.name: Adding an Iceberg catalog implementation
recommended_docs: Subclass IcebergConnectionBase — implement catalog_backend, db_backend_name, settings_class

documentation_plan: Tutorial: add a new Ibis dialect end-to-end (connection builder + DialectSpec + settings class)
Reference: DialectSpec fields and hook signatures
Tutorial: add a new Iceberg catalog type
open_questions: Is there a public stability guarantee for the DialectSpec interface? Can extension authors rely on it not changing?
Should core.registry be the unified extension point once it is wired up?
